newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 20.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
* Banc One Corp is expected to announce its acquisition of First USA Inc in a stock swap worth close to $7 billion, say people familiar with the matter.
* GTE Corp has hired international telecommunications pro Ignacio Santillana to pursue alliances, acquisitions and investments outside the U.S., industry officials said.
* Raytheon Co's pact to buy the defense operations of Hughes Electronics Corp draws attention to a tax-code provision allowing for the deal's tax-free status.
* The new Hughes Electronics Corp should more than double its sales to $10 billion by 2001, its chief executive said.
* Chinese investors have bought Los Angeles's Hotel Inter-Continental for about a third of the $125 million that it cost to build, people familiar with the deal said.
* The trade deficit rose to $8.4 billion in November and industrial production jumped to 0.8 percent in December, the government said.
* Microsoft Corp's net income rose 29 percent in the second quarter, and the company's Windows NT system for computer networks is becoming an important growth engine.
* The Supreme Court will reconsider a government insider-trading weapon that two federal appeals courts had tossed out.
* General Motors Corp is likely to close or sell parts of its Delphi and Delco units as it mergers the operations and prepares them for an intial public offering.
* The Odyssey satellite system partnership of TRW Inc says a Chinese agency has agreed to offer its telephone services.
* Northeast Utilities said two of its units may face bankrupcty filings if New Hampshire's deregulation plan advances.
* Fidelity Investements has formed an alliance with Salomon Brothers to market Salomon stock offerings.
* AMRE Inc said it will file for bankruptcy protection and sell its assets.

* It's been nine months since Roger Enrico took over as chief executive of PepsiCo Inc amid starry expectations for the food and beverate conglomerate. Instead, Enrico has been faced with massive losses at Pepsi's Latin America bottler and sluggish sales at the fast food businesses - Heard on the Street.
* Some savvy bond investors are raising money that they plan to use to snap up distressed debt. Trouble is, there isn't a lot to snap up. -- Credit Markets.
